desc: Build the red graph (adjacency via P) and blue graph (adjacency via Q).
Find the cycle containing X in the red graph and the cycle containing X in the blue graph.
Check if all boxes with $A_i > 0$ are in the red cycle of X, and all boxes with $B_i > 0$ are in the blue cycle of X. If not, print -1.

For the red cycle, determine the set of boxes $S_R$ that need to be operated on. This is the set of boxes $j$ such that $j$ is on the path from some $i$ (with $A_i>0$) to $X$ in the red graph. Specifically, if we define the distance from $i$ to $X$ as the number of steps, the boxes operated on are the starting box and all intermediate boxes up to the one whose P-image is X? No, the last operation is on the box $k$ such that $P_k=X$. The ball moves $k \to X$. So the set $S_R$ is the union of paths from each $i$ with $A_i>0$ to $X$ (including $i$ and excluding $X$? No, we operate on $k$ to move to $X$, so $k$ is included. We don't operate on $X$ to move balls out, we want them to stay. So $X$ is not in $S_R$ unless balls start at $X$ and need to be moved? No, if balls are at $X$, they are already there. We don't operate on $X$.
